newsitem.title: LATVIA: NEW STANDBY AGREEMENT SIGNED WITH IMF.
newsitem.headline: NEW STANDBY AGREEMENT SIGNED WITH IMF.

text.p: Latvian Finance Minister Robert Zile said on Tuesday that a new standby arrangement had been agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

"We have agreed on a new memorandum for 18 months until March 1999. The official signing could take place in September," Zile told a news conference. No details of the size of the standby agreement were given.
An IMF mission has been in Latvia for the last two weeks, assessing Latvia's performance under the previous standby, which was due to expire at the end of August.
Latvia has never used funds from the standby arrangements, which are awarded under various economic criteria agreed with the Fund.

"Given that macroeconomic stability has been achieved to a large extent, the focus of economic policy now shifts to structural reforms to achieve sustainable economic development," IMF head of mission Emmanuel van der Mensbrughe said.
The agreement also says the fiscal deficit should be 0.8 percent by end 1997. Under the conditions of the new standby, efforts will focus on structural reforms in four main areas.
The four areas are attracting more foreign investment by selling large state companies and agreeing on what amount of gross domestic product should be generated by the public sector.
Trade was also part of the agreement, with tariff reductions hoped for. The fourth element was financial sector reform.
"A further deepening of the credit market is necessary," van der Mensbrughe said. He said that further privatisation of land was also needed.
